review_kind: Codex-assisted answer review; not a human review or paid LLM-judge run
criteria_policy: Exact frozen descriptions and all-three-plus-no-material-defect task-pass rule retained; historical baseline results are not modified.
scope: First recorded UI answers only. Inspect answer text, cited snapshot passages, Python syntax and behavior statically. No generated-code execution, paid judge calls, or remote product integrations.

criteria.description: Explains the distinct roles of tracing, dataset-based evaluation, and Signals and how they can be used together.
criteria.reason: Explains tracing as the activity record, Evaluations as repeatable dataset-based tests, and Signals as scores/tags on traced conversations. The relationships are clear despite unusually cautious inference wording.

criteria.description: Explains that Signals score completed turns; does not confuse their execution timing with an inline answer-release check.
criteria.reason: The delivered answer never states that Signals score completed turns. It does not assert inline answer gating, but omission still fails the unchanged timing criterion.

criteria.description: Does not claim monitoring prevents errors, proves correctness, or guarantees safety.
criteria.reason: No prevention, correctness or safety guarantee is made; the answer limits itself to observation, measurement and attention.

tasks.source_review: The material role, data-model and API claims are supported by the cited read passages. The tracing-to-Signals relationship is a reasonable explicitly labelled synthesis. No material false claim demonstrated.
caveats: Criterion a2 requires completed-turn timing beyond the literal broad question. The answer is a useful high-level overview and satisfies its narrower runtime task plan; the frozen 2/3 grade is not a claim that the answer is useless.
The runtime complete label and the external frozen rubric measure different task scope after the prompt repair. Historical baseline grades remain unchanged.

criteria.description: Recommends appropriate Op input/output postprocessing hooks to change recorded representations without changing the business function.
criteria.reason: Names postprocess_inputs and postprocess_output on @weave.op and explains their effect on recorded representations.

criteria.description: Explains that the input callback receives and returns an argument dictionary, while the output callback transforms the normal return value.
criteria.reason: Correctly states that the input hook accepts/returns an argument dictionary and the output hook transforms the normal return value.

criteria.description: Describes a suitable masking or omission approach that preserves the real function inputs and behavior. Code is optional; supplied code must implement the described behavior.
criteria.reason: The supplied code filters the logged-input copy and constructs a new masked output object. The business function still receives hide_me and returns its normal object. The annotation and keyword expressions are intact.

tasks.source_review: The code and hook contracts follow guides/tracking/ops section 3. The TypeScript limitation is explicitly scoped to that page. No material unsupported claim demonstrated.
tasks.code_behavior_review: Input dictionary comprehension omits hide_me without mutating the function inputs; output callback returns a separate CustomObject with REDACTED while func builds the normal result. Code matches the documented example; no execution performed.
caveats: Static review and Python parsing establish no remote logging behavior or production privacy guarantee.

criteria.description: Explains the mapping from dataset fields to agent or prediction inputs and from predictions plus relevant reference fields to scorer inputs.
criteria.reason: The task dictionary enters log_prediction(inputs=task); task["user_request"] goes to run_agent_turn, whose reply is pred.output. The judge receives the task including its success criteria and the generated transcript.

criteria.description: Gives a usable documented evaluation invocation or concrete API-level procedure; accept equivalent supported APIs rather than requiring one particular evaluation class.
criteria.reason: Shows the documented EvaluationLogger/log_prediction/log_score/log_summary procedure. The code is explicitly an adapted fragment with helpers supplied by the linked tutorial, rather than a standalone runnable program.

criteria.description: Describes a task-relevant LLM judge rubric and how its scores or reasons are recorded or reviewed, without presenting the verdict as certain. An unsolicited fallibility lecture is not required.
criteria.reason: Describes a task-completion judge comparing transcript to the request and success criteria, returning passed and reason, and records its result through pred.log_score. Explains how to inspect passed verdicts and compare versions without claiming certainty.

tasks.source_review: Evaluation loop and judge contracts directly follow agent-evals section 4; version comparison follows section 5.
tasks.code_behavior_review: Static mapping and documented APIs are coherent. The snippet leaves tasks, imports and helper implementations to the cited tutorial and does not claim standalone execution.
caveats: Minor wording imprecision: start_conversation is a Weave SDK function imported elsewhere in the tutorial, whereas new_id and run_agent_turn are application helpers. This does not prevent the documented procedure.
No generated code, model judge or remote evaluation was executed by this review.

criteria.description: Across both turns, retains the direct-Anthropic, Python, custom-loop context and gives appropriate conversation/turn/model/tool instrumentation; does not confuse tracing identity with LLM memory.
criteria.reason: Both turns retain Python, direct Anthropic and the custom-loop context. The answer gives conversation/turn/model/tool instrumentation and refers back to the earlier sketch. Conversation identity is not presented as LLM memory.

criteria.description: Explains how to record model identity and input, output, cache-read, and cache-creation usage on the model span using suitable documented APIs or adapters; does not silently switch to an OpenAI-only response schema.
criteria.reason: The follow-up records Anthropic input/output/cache-read/cache-creation fields through Usage and llm.record, with response_model=resp.model and response_id. It places this on each model-call span and does not switch to an OpenAI response schema.

criteria.description: Handles provider-to-Weave input totals without double counting cache tokens, distinguishes cached categories where available, and does not fabricate exact dollar costs. If conversation or tool-call code is supplied, it must preserve the relevant preceding assistant messages.
criteria.reason: The formula includes uncached input plus cache-read plus cache-creation exactly once, preserves the two cache categories and output count, and invents no exact dollar cost. The supplied examples are explicitly fragments with placeholder history, not a full tool loop; they do not construct an incorrect assistant/tool message sequence.

tasks.source_review: The first-turn nesting/initialization sketch follows agent-evals section 3; the op alternative follows Threads definitions. Follow-up accounting follows custom-agents-quickstart section 8. Its retained conversation_context contains the exact preceding user/assistant exchange.
tasks.code_behavior_review: Both Python fragments parse. The first is explicitly not a complete loop; the second carries the history placeholder through messages=history and does not modify it. Inclusive input accounting is correct and separate cached categories are retained. Weave top-level and weave.conversation Usage imports are both valid in the installed SDK.
caveats: Minor source-imprecision repeated by the answer: Conversation groups turns by conversation_id and does not itself emit a span, despite agent-evals wording about a Conversation span. The actual nesting and duplicate-instrumentation caution remain useful.

The copied text-only example accesses resp.content[0].text. A first tool-use or thinking block requires adaptation before the usage record; the answer explicitly limits itself to text and says tool-use handling was not checked. This is not a complete custom-loop implementation.
Like the source example, cache values are added directly rather than normalized with or 0. Nullable SDK values would need defensive handling; no failing response was executed in this protocol.

No generated code, provider request or remote trace export executed by this review. Complete assistant/tool-history preservation is not demonstrated by these fragments; no invalid history sequence is supplied.

cache_arithmetic_review.scope: Illustrates the supplied formula; not measured usage or execution of generated code.

criteria.description: Does not present weave.enable_hallucination_free_mode() as a real supported API; scopes documentation absence claims to the evidence available.
criteria.reason: Explicitly declines to invent the requested API signature and scopes the absence claim to the Weave documentation searched.
Rejects the never-hallucinate premise: no documented guarantee is claimed, and the conclusion says a scorer measures rather than prevents hallucination.

summary.decision: Five of six tasks satisfy the unchanged frozen criteria; all seven turns delivered answers. The only failed outcome is the overview completed-turn timing omission.
summary.qualifications: Useful overview despite a stricter-than-literal frozen timing criterion; instrumentation examples remain explicitly incomplete and text-only. A Conversation is grouping rather than an emitted span. No generated code or remote integration executed.
summary.comparison_limit: Reused tasks, one repair attempt each, multiple changes and model nondeterminism; these records do not isolate a causal quality or latency effect. Baseline grades and Claude answers are preserved.
